summary: Aggregation window resonance causing p95/p99 latency bursts on dedicated cluster
description: Issue summary: Several customers on a dedicated cluster (LexiHealth) reported reproducible p95/p99 inference latency spikes and intermittent 504s during sustained steady traffic. Spikes align with ~10s periodicity and frequently occur at the same wall-clock offsets across many connections. Impact: Production inference for LexiHealth experienced ~15% of requests hitting p99 > 2.5s during windows, causing degraded user experience for symptom-check flows. Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-west, serving-runtime v1.3.8, scheduler v2.0.2, adaptive batching enabled with default idle estimator. Observed behavior: Periodic bursts where aggregation window appears to 'resonate' — requests queue up slightly longer than expected, then flush in a larger-than-normal batch causing downstream KV cache misses and transient CPU/GPU contention leading to p95/p99 regressions. Timing shows alignment with the adaptive idle estimator's oscillation interval after a recent optimizer tweak.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision dedicated cluster with same config as LexiHealth (4 nodes, adaptive batching enabled, idle_estimator=adaptive-v2).
2) Replay production traffic trace (steady 8 qps with short sequences, token length distribution attached) for 20 minutes.
3) Observe latency histograms in serving runtime and scheduler dashboards; periodic p99 spikes at ~10s intervals should appear.
4) Toggle idle_estimator to adaptive-v1 and re-run; spike pattern mitigates in our test runs.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor or GPU saturation — ruled out by per-GPU utilization graphs (no sustained saturation during spikes).
Correlation observed between coalescer window oscillation and latency spikes; window_ms drifts +/- 25ms around a nominal value causing alignment of many connections for a brief instant.
KV cache miss rate increases during flushes due to larger-than-expected batch sizes with mixed sequence lengths; cache warmup couldn't amortize cost for those flush sizes.
Replayed traffic in staging: switching idle_estimator back to adaptive-v1 removed the periodicity and reduced p99 by ~40% under the same load.
A recent change (serving-runtime commit 9f3d2a8) adjusted the estimator damping factor; likely introduced resonance in specific QPS/sequence-length regimes.
comments: Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer noticed tail latency spikes at roughly 10s intervals after yesterday's autoscaler tuning. Provided logs and sample traces.
Marcus Lee (SRE) 2026-03-12: Reproduced in staging. Attaching trace and CPU/GPU utilization. Suspect adaptive idle estimator oscillation.
Priya Nambiar (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-13: Found commit 9f3d2a8 that changed estimator damping. Putting a rollback candidate together and testing.
Marcus Lee (SRE) 2026-03-13: Applied a temporary mitigation (pin idle_estimator=adaptive-v1) to LexiHealth's config — observed p99 drop back to baseline. Informing customer and monitoring.
resolution: Workaround applied: pinned customer cluster's idle_estimator to adaptive-v1 and temporarily increased batch flush jitter to break alignment. Partial mitigation deployed to LexiHealth prod (2026-03-13 22:10 UTC) — p99 returned to baseline in monitoring. Root cause: estimator damping change in serving-runtime introduced a resonance in aggregation window under LexiHealth's QPS / sequence-length distribution. Full fix: PR (serving-runtime #3512) includes adaptive damping with hysteresis and a unit test to reproduce resonance; scheduled for canary on 2026-03-15.
follow_up_items: Merge PR 3512 and run canary on non-critical dedicated pools (owner: Priya) — target 2026-03-15.
Add synthetic load test that exercises estimator oscillation patterns to CI to prevent regressions (owner: Runtime QE).
Create dashboard tile showing coalescer window variance and correlation with p99 for early detection (owner: Marcus).
Notify other dedicated customers who received serving-runtime v1.3.8 about potential transient tail spikes and recommended mitigation (Support).
